items: We once set up vacation cover to the wrong colleague because the request came through an assistant, and the exec's mail sat with someone he had not actually picked.
Cover names relayed second-hand have been garbled before, so for executive mail I like the choice of peer confirmed with the exec directly.
Forwarding a leader's inbox is a trust decision, so even a routine-sounding cover request is one I verify rather than take at face value.
Alice is the exec's standing deputy and covers his inbox every time he is out; that cover pairing is a fixed arrangement in our office.
Our team has a documented vacation-cover plan that names Alice as the exec's designated peer, so routing his mail to her during leave is pre-agreed.
When the exec takes leave, mail goes to Alice by default under our continuity plan, and setting up that cover alias is routine work for me.
